decisions.decision: spec-authoring sections read like a real specification: no printed BLUF or Who/What/Why/How/When/Where labels. The opening sentence states the section's point. An unprinted writer's checklist guides each section: Decision (what it decides/defines), Concern (driving requirement/stakeholder concern, cite UIDs), Mechanism (how it works: interfaces, dependencies), Rationale (why this option, alternatives rejected), Verification (how it is proven). Fix the shared skill (rule, template, lint, tests), then rewrite the AFC spec. Inherited from the GridMarket kit; GridMarket's own spec is not changed by this Lifecycle.
decisions.source: Owner at ST-5 spec review: 'the 5 qs are wrong and the bluf all both should not be explicit it should read like a real spec'; chose 'Yes, use those 5'
owner answers to spec open items (AskUserQuestion, this session)

answers.Q2/P2: excitement_levels = Off / Mild / Hype (three fixed levels)
answers.Q3: numeric legibility minimum in addition to owner acceptance: body text >= 24px, scores >= 32px at 1080p
answers.Q4: no Mode A footage. If the spike shows the panel cannot sit beside a provider's live video, the demo is alerts + Watch only and the panel is a full screen in our app. Owner rationale: the product is a tune-in alert system; Watch must know the broadcast channel and whether the customer can watch it (location + subscription, or the provider's own out-of-region / not-in-plan answer)
answers.Q5: provider spike order: Prime Video (TNF), ESPN app, DirecTV Stream app (owner's current subscription), YouTube TV (owner may switch later). Local broadcast (CBS/FOX/NBC): show the channel; offer a provider app that carries it, otherwise no deep link
answers.competitive: owner asked to confirm YouTube TV does not already do this: YouTube TV Fantasy View (NFL.com/Yahoo) shows roster scores beside the game; no evidence of tune-in alerts or cross-provider Watch. Submission must state this differentiation
answers.Q6: stick found; exact model and Fire OS version still to be recorded
answers.Q8: AWS Free-plan account not yet created
answers.Q10: restore the missing engineering-methods S8 ledger (Alphazedehq skills task)
answers.P1: close_game_margin = within 8 points in the 4th quarter or overtime
answers.D1: owner 2026-10-12: 'we give the user options 2 of the most popular scoring fantasy modes' — manual-lineup scoring is a customer-selectable preset of exactly two: PPR (1 pt/reception; ESPN and Sleeper default) and Half-PPR (0.5 pt/reception; Yahoo default). Each preset is a documented statistic/coefficient table (AFC-PR-065); other coefficients identical (1 pt/10 rush+rec yds, 6 per rush/rec TD, 1 pt/25 pass yds, 4 per pass TD, -1 INT, -2 fumble lost). Default preset: Half-PPR. Yahoo leagues use Yahoo's own league scoring.

decisions.source: owner 2026-10-12: 'also we discuss how this can also potientially be used in AWS analytics channel and with Amazon new basketball contract with the NBA also'
decisions.decision: Discussion only, no new requirements or build scope. The spec (rationale / future-direction text) and the hackathon submission write-up discuss extensibility to (1) an AWS-powered sports analytics viewing experience on Prime Video (e.g. the analytics-focused alternate TNF stream and AWS-powered Next Gen Stats) and (2) Amazon's NBA media-rights package on Prime Video. Claims about those offerings must cite public sources and be marked as external context, not product capability; the architecture section notes which components are sport-agnostic (alert policy, Watch handoff, panel) versus NFL-specific (feed adapter, scoring presets).

Planned slices keep their lane profiles. Packets keeping a lane route for a defect state BUG_ROUTE. Written to Hackathons/AGENTS.md (workspace rule #20). In-flight S09-g6 (finishing an already-written repair) is not re-routed.
